rationale: The step's entire NCCL work is exactly 13 c10d::allreduce_ calls (group f833b57a373d8262a384: 12x 7,087,872-element fp32 buckets; group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0: 1x 39,385,344-element embedding bucket; 497,759,232 B total, RING_LL on stream 17, both ranks, call parents only the project invoke). DDP flags, bytes, algorithm and transport are frozen, and faster local compute kernels cannot move a summed-NCCL-kernel-duration metric, so the only evidenced reducible term is in-kernel spin-wait: the separately collected collective_calibration at exactly these sizes/dtypes with synchronized ranks measures a floor of 12x3.593 + 19.642 = ~62.8 ms per rank, while the clean original baseline objective is 74.676 ms max-rank (rank 1: 64.149), i.e. ~11.9 ms of the metric is device waiting, not transfer. The current execution_timeline pins the mechanism: cross-rank CPU submission spread is 6.25 ms already at the first collective (seq 21) and grows only ~1 ms to 7.29 ms by the last (seq 33) - the offset is accumulated over the host dispatch of the pre-collective part of the step and then held inside every NCCL kernel as spin-wait; skew growth inside the collective sequence itself is small. The previous execution_plan candidate (trial-df7761708a, whole-step CUDA graph) is the concrete failure to repair: its capture never engaged - both tiers raised RuntimeError ('Cannot copy between CPU and CUDA tensors during CUDA graph capture unless the CPU tensor is pinned' from transformers masking_utils.eager_mask via aten scalar creation), fell back to eager, and the fallback run breached the step_ms constraint (139.370 ms vs 138.660 limit) with inflated allocator state (reserved 3.24 GB vs 2.10 GB baseline, lifecycle peak 4.08 GB) from snapshots and failed graph pools; its observed 64.01 ms communication value is therefore not evidence of replay, only of the metric's run-to-run range (64-80 ms). The minimal coherent boundary for a different mechanism is the allreduce dispatch itself: both call sites must be edited together because the first collective of a step can be dispatched through either site (12+1 invocations per step, DDP bucket rebuild after iteration 1 may permute order), and the per-step alignment point is 'first allreduce_ invocation of the final backward'. A joint functional replacement over both sites - a pass-through that calls the parent with identical arguments, preceded once per step (shared 13-count across both sites) by a rank-symmetric gloo barrier (lazily created gloo group; no NCCL kernel, no metric cost) at that first dispatch - removes the accumulated arrival offset from the NCCL kernels. No DDP communication hook is registered, no DDP flag, byte, algorithm, operator order or numerical path changes: the same 13 parent allreduce_ calls execute through context.references with identical tensors, so gradients stay bit-exact replicas and reference checks are unaffected. Unlike the rejected graph plan there is no capture, no extra memory, no setup invocation, and no per-replay coverage ambiguity; the ~13 Python dispatch hops plus one barrier add well under 1 ms of host work per 132 ms step.
hypothesis: Aligning both ranks at the first bucket-allreduce dispatch of each step's final backward collapses the ~6.25-7.29 ms cross-rank submission offset that currently sits inside every NCCL kernel as spin-wait, so per-kernel durations fall to the calibrated transfer floor (12x~3.6 ms + ~19.6 ms) plus only the ~1 ms residual growth observed across the collective sequence. The max-rank communication_kernel_sum_ms should drop from the 74.676 ms baseline toward ~63-66 ms (roughly 9-12 ms, ~12-16%), with the median-of-3 profiled protocol damping the observed 64-80 ms run-to-run variance. step_ms should stay within the 138.66 ms limit (~132-134 ms expected): the barrier converts the early rank's former device spin-wait into a host wait of similar length while the trailing rank - which already paces both ranks' nearly identical baseline step walls (131.91/132.06 ms) - is unaffected, and the collectives themselves still synchronize the ranks before optimizer.step(). Unknowns to be tested, not assumed: (a) under the torch_communication profiler the residual skew growth within the final backward may exceed the timeline-observed ~1 ms, bounding the gain short of the floor; (b) gloo barrier latency (~sub-ms plus store rendezvous on first use) adds directly to step wall on the early rank; (c) the 13-calls-per-step invariant (12 small + 1 embedding bucket, stable set under bucket rebuild) is assumed and guarded by counting across both sites - any deviation would misplace the barrier, so the installed candidate must verify the per-step collective inventory; (d) the objective's run-to-run spread means acceptance depends on the measured median, not on any single predicted value.
